newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open mostly higher.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open mostly higher Wednesday, led by platinum group metals (PGMs).
Overnight, Russian metal export agency Almaz said in a statement Russia would resume exports of PGMs at the "nearest" possible time and confirmed it remained the sole Russian PGM exporter.
Earlier, it had said spot sales would resume June 20 and contract supplies to Japan would resume in July. There had also been indications the Russian central bank was now involved in PGM exports.

Overnight, Japanese traders said they had signed deals for July-December delivery of PGMs from Russia and said they had been advised Almaz had now received its long-delayed export licence. Russian PGM exports have been suspended for five months, causing an acute shortage of the white metals.

But separately, Russia's financially troubled Norilsk Nickel metal group, which produces most of Russia's PGMs, said overnight it had sacked the director of its precious metals processing plant and no replacement was named.
NYMEX July platinum was called up $2.00 to $3.00 from Tuesday's close of $438.90 an ounce after three days of declines.
NYMEX September palladium was called up the same from the previous close of $173.80.

COMEX August gold was called unchanged to off $.20 from Tuesday's close of $346.10, although support from a weaker dollar was likely, analysts said. The dollar fell to a seven-month low against yen overnight.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks were unchanged at 967,026 ounces Tuesday.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $343.65/95 early against the London morning fix of $343.70 and Tuesday's New York close of $343.70/$344.20.
COMEX July silver was called unchanged to up 0.50 cent from the previous close of $4.745.
COMEX silver stocks fell 3,648,065 ounces to 200,334,290 ounces Tuesday.
